title: Count in 2s, 5s and 10s
summary: Name the step, count back, spot a number you would not say, and order backwards.
subject: maths

difficultyRamp.within: Q1 counts back in twos from 20. Child subtracts 2, not 1. Q2 picks 16, a number you would not say in fives. Q3 counts 4 children holding up two hands each in tens. Q4 names the step in 15, 20, 25, 30. Q5 finds 30 counting back in tens. Q6 picks two numbers you would not say in tens. Q7 matches 40 to the word forty. Q8 continues 25, 20, 15 counting back in fives. Q9 fills 70 on a hundred square. Q10 orders 50, 45, 40, 35 from biggest to smallest.
difficultyRamp.versus: Easy uses pairs and tens pictures up to 50, with hops on the number line. Medium adds fives, a twos gap, a tens pick and higher 5s counts. Hard names the step size, counts back, spots a number you would not say, and orders from biggest to smallest. Hard is a new kind of thinking, not just bigger numbers.
